summary.headline: Lumax Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 1,364 crore, with EBITDA up 51% at a 15.1% margin and PAT up 83% to INR 99 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR 1,364 crore grew 33% y-o-y, with EBITDA of INR 205 crore (up 51%, margin 15.1%, up 190 bps) and PAT of INR 99 crore (up 83%). Management said the margin would hold for the rest of the year, and guidance was kept unchanged: 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 and about 20% revenue CAGR. Growth was helped by a low base and industry production up 22% y-o-y, but management expects growth to slow in Q3 and Q4 after the post-GST-rationalisation base effect. The order book stands at INR 1,600 crore, with about 24% expected in FY27, 56% in FY28 and 20% in FY29.

segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC, ~60% share of division)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 47% y-o-y from INR 525 crore to INR 769 crore; order book INR 787 crore. Division is more than half of group revenue; margin band 16-20%.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: Revenue rose ~56% y-o-y from INR 54 crore to INR 84 crore; order book close to INR 500 crore. Management expects ~INR 400 crore FY27 revenue and ~INR 1,000 crore by FY31; currently 6-7% of group.

segments.name: Structure and Control Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 21% y-o-y from INR 180 crore to INR 220 crore; order book INR 130 crore.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% y-o-y from INR 98 crore to INR 104 crore, hit by non-lighting products and pricing; management still guides for double-digit growth for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 17% y-o-y from INR 95 crore to INR 111 crore; order book INR 200 crore. Q1 EBITDA margin was ~23%, including ~3% one-off tooling revenue; underlying ~20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance is unchanged: about 20% revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31 vision) and EBITDA margin of about 15% for FY27; management expects Q1 margins of 15.1% to be sustained for the rest of the year.

FY27 capex guided at about INR 300 crore, including Mechatronics greenfield and new IAC plants; Q1 capex was INR 23 crore. About 10-12% of capex may be debt-funded at JV or subsidiary level; the rest from internal accruals.

Targets: FY28 EBITDA about INR 1,000 crore, implying 15.5-16% margin (including other income); longer term, move toward 20% EBITDA margin over 5-7 years, with 17-17.5% cited as a satisfactory interim outcome.
Mechatronics JVs to operate at 14-15% EBITDA over the next 12-24 months; Greenfuel margin range 19-20%.
Aftermarket: management expects growth of 15% or more versus 10-12% under the earlier strategy.
Minority interest expected at 11-13% of PAT. Inorganic growth not planned for the current year, but strategic fits are being evaluated.
capex_capacity: New IAC plant at Chakan for Mahindra & Mahindra demand, with some product-line optimisation across facilities.
Mega Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, expected to commission by Q3 FY27; consolidates Lumax Yokowo, Lumax Alps Alpine, Lumax Ituran and Lumax FAE.
Greenfuel to set up a new facility in Nashik to serve Mahindra (passenger vehicle CNG delivery system).
FY27 capex guidance of INR 300 crore; order book of INR 1,600 crore to be served on this spend for FY28 and FY29 needs. Capex may be revised for FY28 if order book grows.
SHIFT centre in Bangalore for software-defined vehicles and ADAS development.
demand_pricing: Industry: production up 22% y-o-y in Q1 FY27 (PV +17% to 14.5 lakh, CV +15% to ~3 lakh, 2W +23% to 72.5 lakh, 3W +39% to 3.5 lakh); management expects slower growth in Q3-Q4 because of the high FY26 base.
Plastics prices rose ~30-40%; 80-90% of the increase is passed through to OEMs within the same quarter under back-to-back arrangements, with spillover to the next quarter for a few OEMs.
Electronics components rose by more than 30-50% in some cases; the low Mechatronics share limits the margin impact.
Maruti Suzuki revenue grew 48% y-o-y in Q1; Bajaj Auto revenue grew ~64% y-o-y, attributed to wallet-share gains and new models.
Aftermarket growth was held back by pricing: competitors absorbed input-cost increases while Lumax passed them on in non-lighting categories.
Order book: ~one-third sits with IAC, mostly Mahindra. Order book across verticals: Advanced Plastics first, then Mechatronics, Alternate Fuels and Structures and Control Systems.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company revising FY27 guidance given 33% top-line growth and strong Q1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept unchanged. Q1 and Q2 sit on a low base, so growth looks robust now, but growth rates will slow sharply in Q3 and Q4 after the high post-GST-rationalisation FY26 base. Q1 margins of 15.1% expected to be sustained for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How has Lumax managed margins despite plastics up ~30-40%, and how are OEM pass-throughs timed?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastics are on back-to-back OEM arrangements; 80-90% of the increase is recovered within the same quarter, with spillover to the next quarter for a few OEMs. H2 FY26 margin was ~14.9%. Electronics inflation (30-50%+ in some components) has limited impact because Mechatronics is only 6-7% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfuel's Q1 margin of ~23% — one-off or operational? What is the Mahindra business?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 3 crore of one-off tooling revenue from an existing customer, roughly 3% of margin. Normalised operational EBITDA is ~20%, and 19-20% is the expected range. The Mahindra win is for a passenger-vehicle CNG delivery system, not LCVs.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Bajaj Auto's ~64% revenue growth against much lower volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to wallet-share expansion and new models, including new frames for other models. The metallics division grew ~37-40% in Q1, and Chetak is a key platform for both lighting and frames.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected Mechatronics wallet share and growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: No market-share number given. Management targets top-2 positions in connectivity products such as shark-fin antennas within 3-5 years, and top-2 in switches and sensors within 3 years. FY27 Mechatronics revenue is guided at ~INR 400 crore, rising to ~INR 1,000 crore by FY31. Order book is INR 400-500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Minority interest outlook, and is the 20% CAGR now organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority interest guided at 11-13% of PAT, given the current structure after the IAC merger and Lumax FAE becoming a 100% subsidiary. Management said 15% organic CAGR plus a few hundred crore of inorganic was the earlier framework; 20% CAGR is still maintained, but no inorganic deal is planned this year.

risks_watch: Growth deceleration in Q3-Q4 FY27 as the post-GST-rationalisation base effect bites; management did not give a revised full-year revenue figure.
Margin durability: the 15.1% Q1 EBITDA margin relies on same-quarter plastics pass-through (80-90%), and electronics inflation (30-50%+ in some parts) could lag or hit Mechatronics as it scales.

Aftermarket: Q1 growth of 6% was hit by pricing in non-lighting categories where competitors absorbed costs; management targets 15%+ for the rest of the year, which needs to be seen. OEM push into aftermarket is also a stated pressure.
JV profitability: management says no JV is EBITDA-negative now, but one JV is still marginally loss-making at PBT; Mechatronics JVs are guided to 14-15% EBITDA only over 12-24 months.
Order book concentration: about one-third of the order book sits with IAC, mostly Mahindra; diversification to Maruti and Honda is guided to take until FY28.
Capex execution: FY27 capex guidance of INR 300 crore against INR 23 crore spent in Q1 requires a steep ramp; Manesar mega plant due by Q3 FY27 and Chakan and Nashik plants.
key_quotes: As of now, we continue with the similar guidance.
On the margin front, I think I can only say that we will be able to sustain these current margins achieved in Q1 for the remaining part of the year as well.
Not because the demand will slow down, but purely because of the base becoming significantly higher in FY 26 post the GST rationalization.
Number one, Pritesh, I do not think we have ever said that we will attain 20%. It is more of a direction that we would like to inch closer to a 20% margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and long-term targets, but deliberately cautious on the full-year outlook: guidance was held rather than raised and management flagged slower growth in H2. Evasive on specifics such as Mechatronics market share, the Advanced Plastics margin split and the one-off Greenfuel item, which were addressed only partly and with qualifiers.
